source: HousingWire, NAR and Inside Mortgage Finance

headline: VA loan fees could
*nearly triple*
slides.fig_caption: Proposed fee on VA streamline refinances (IRRRLs), up from 0.5%
slides.sub: A House-passed veterans bill would pay for new benefits by raising fees on VA refinances and loan assumptions.

slides.kicker: Fee as a share of the loan
slides.title: Now vs. *proposed*
slides.note: The assumption fee would *double*. Current purchase and cash-out funding fees would be extended for nondisabled veterans.

slides.label: estimated added cost over the life of a *$400,000* VA loan
slides.body: That estimate comes from a mortgage broker coalition, which says the breakeven on a VA streamline refi would stretch from about 1.5 years to about 5.

slides.title: Next stop: *the Senate*
points: H.R. 9237 passed the House by voice vote on Veterans Day, bundled into a package of 60 veterans measures.
The fee hikes come from H.R. 6047, which cleared the House in June and then stalled in the Senate.
House VA Committee Chair Mike Bost of Illinois says he aims to get it to the president by year-end.
NAR backs the benefits but has asked lawmakers to strip out the fee increases.

slides.title: Nothing changes *yet*
slides.body: If it becomes law, buyers taking over a seller's low-rate VA loan would pay twice the assumption fee, and veteran clients weighing a streamline refi would wait longer to break even. Worth watching before year-end.
